advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Wrap the new checks_for_repo lookup in analyze_ci_failure so a checks-config error degrades to an empty fix_command hint instead of failing the activity.
evidence: services/orchestration/temporal_activities/repair.py:55: `config = checks_for_repo(req.repo, settings) if req.repo else None`
services/orchestration/checks/config.py:66: `configs[str(repo)] = parse_checks_config(str(repo), entry)` — parse raises ConfigError
Unlike _project_autofix (which wraps failures in try/except and degrades), analyze_ci_failure has no guard around the new checks_for_repo call.
advisory.finding: analyze_ci_failure now calls checks_for_repo(req.repo, settings) unconditionally (when repo is set) without a try/except, whereas the analyze activity previously never touched the checks config. load_checks_configs / parse_checks_configs raises ConfigError on a malformed or invalid checks.yaml, which will now fail the analyze_ci_failure activity for a purely cosmetic reason (fetching a fix_command hint), degrading a previously config-independent path.
scenarios: A repo's checks.yaml has an invalid entry (missing command / bad mapping) — analyze_ci_failure now raises instead of just planning the repair.
advisory.suggested_fix: Guard the lookup: `try: config = checks_for_repo(req.repo, settings) if req.repo else None; except Exception: config = None`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the fix_command exit status in _fix_inner_script and surface it so a failed fixer is distinguishable from a clean run.
evidence: services/orchestration/checks/runner.py:129: `spec.fix_command,` — run inline, no `$?` capture
services/orchestration/checks/runner.py:142-145: only `verify_rc=$?` for `spec.command` is captured and returned via `exit $verify_rc`
The inner script is executed with `sh` (not `sh -e`), so a nonzero fix_command does not abort the script.
advisory.finding: In _fix_inner_script the project's fix_command exit status is never captured or checked; the script proceeds to the manifest step and check re-run regardless. A fix command that partially fails (e.g. `npm ci` fails before the formatter runs) is only detected if the subsequent verify re-run happens to fail. The final exit code reported to run_fix is verify_rc alone, so a fix that errored yet left the checks passing (or a check that is insensitive to the failure) is reported as a successful verified fix.
scenarios: fix_command does dependency setup then a formatter; setup fails but checks still pass by coincidence — reported as a verified applied fix.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the privileged-pod escalation is reviewed for security implications given it runs untrusted project fix_commands.
evidence: services/orchestration/gates/pod_runner.py: `if privileged: security_context["privileged"] = True`
scripts/config.py:127: `gate_engine_privileged: bool = False`
repair.py passes `privileged=settings.gate_engine_privileged` into the pod running the untrusted project fix_command.
advisory.finding: build_pod_manifest now can set securityContext.privileged=True driven by gate_engine_privileged. A privileged container disables most container isolation (full device access, host kernel capabilities). While defaulted False, this is a substantial security posture change and the wiring (builtin.py, checks activity, repair autofix) propagates it into the CI-repair pod that runs arbitrary project fix_commands.
scenarios: An operator enables gate_engine_privileged on a shared cluster; the pod running arbitrary repo fix_commands gains privileged host access.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a planner test asserting `plan_repair(lint_summary, fix_command='npm run format').instruction` contains `run \`npm run format\`` and that the empty-fix_command case omits it.
evidence: ci_repair.py adds: `fix_hint = (f" The project declares its own fix command, so run \`{fix_command}\` before editing by hand." if fix_command else "")` and formats it into the LINT instruction template
plan_repair/analyze_failure gained `fix_command: str = ""` parameters (added `+` lines)
search of tests/unit for `fix_hint` returns (no matches); tests/unit/test_ci_repair_planner.py has no test passing fix_command to plan_repair/analyze_failure

Named violating input: `plan_repair('app.py:1:1: E501 ...', fix_command='npm run format')` — the added lines produce an instruction whose hint content is never asserted, so a regression dropping or malforming the hint would go undetected.
advisory.finding: The newly added `fix_hint` behavior in `_plan`/`plan_repair`/`analyze_failure` is untested: no test asserts that passing `fix_command` injects the `run \`<cmd>\`` hint into the LINT instruction, nor that it is absent when `fix_command` is empty.
scenarios: A refactor that drops fix_hint from the LINT template, or passes fix_command but fails to interpolate it, ships green.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a run_fix test with a fake PodOps that returns exit 0 and GATEFIX markers, asserting copy_out is called with the manifest path and ChecksFixResult(verified=True, changed_files=...).
evidence: run_fix added with branch `if code == 0 and changed: await self._ops.copy_out(...)` and `verified=code == 0 and bool(changed)` (runner.py:252-260)
The only run_fix test asserts the early return: tests/unit/test_ci_repair_project_fix.py:70 `test_run_fix_reports_unverified_when_no_fix_command_is_declared` with `ChecksRunner(object())`
search of tests/unit for `copy_out` returns (no matches); KubectlPodOps.copy_out and _copy_out_sync (pod_runner.py:293-327, added) have no test

Named violating input: a fake PodOps returning exec_capture=(0, output with GATEFIX_FILES markers, '') — run_fix should call copy_out and set verified=True/changed_files, but no test asserts copy_out is invoked or that verified reflects code/changed.
advisory.finding: ChecksRunner.run_fix's happy path (exit code 0 with changed files, driving copy_out) and KubectlPodOps.copy_out/_copy_out_sync are untested; the only run_fix test exercises the empty-fix_command early return, so the create/wait/copy_in/exec/parse/copy_out orchestration and the tar-pipe error handling never run under test.
scenarios: A regression inverting the `code == 0 and changed` copy_out guard, or setting verified incorrectly, ships green.
The untar error-handling (`if untar.returncode or exec_proc.returncode`) never executes in tests.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Harden host-side `tar xmf` in `_copy_out_sync` against symlink/path traversal (e.g. extract with GNU tar's traversal protections and refuse symlink members, or validate members before writing) since the archive is built from untrusted pod-controlled content.
evidence: `untar = subprocess.Popen(["tar", "xmf", "-", "--no-same-owner", "-C", dest_dir], stdin=exec_proc.stdout)` (pod_runner.py:319-321) — no `--no-absolute-names`/traversal or symlink guard

tar payload is generated inside the pod from a manifest the untrusted fix command populated: `tar cf - --ignore-failed-read -C {source_dir} -T {manifest_path}` (pod_runner.py:310-312); manifest lines come from `find ... -newer .gatefix.marker` after `spec.fix_command` runs (runner.py:129-136)
The _confined()/scope checks in `_apply_staged_files` run only after extraction into `staging` (repair.py:214-228), so they cannot prevent an escape that occurs during `tar xmf` itself
advisory.finding: Host-side tar extraction of the pod's changed-file archive is not hardened against symlink/path traversal; the tar stream is produced by the untrusted project fix command inside the pod, and `tar xmf - -C dest_dir` will follow symlink entries in the archive to write files outside dest_dir on the orchestration worker, before the later _confined()/scope guards run.
scenarios: A repo whose declared fix_command (or a compromised dependency it installs) emits a tar-visible symlink such as `link -> /home/worker/.ssh` plus `link/authorized_keys`, causing host-side extraction to write through the symlink outside the staging dir

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the GATEFIX_VERIFY_RC marker was emitted (and equals 0) before treating a fix as verified, rather than trusting the outer process exit code alone.
evidence: services/orchestration/checks/runner.py:194: `if line.startswith(_VERIFY_RC): continue` — marker dropped, never returned
services/orchestration/checks/runner.py:250 region: run_fix uses `code == 0 and changed` for verified, where `code` is exec_capture's exit code, not the parsed verify_rc
`inner = f"echo {b64} | base64 -d | sh"` — the inner sh's exit propagates through the pipe, but nothing confirms the VERIFY_RC line was actually emitted.
dropped.finding: parse_fix_output parses and then discards the GATEFIX_VERIFY_RC=<n> marker line, and run_fix trusts the buildah process exit code (`code`) as the verification signal instead of the parsed verify_rc. If buildah/the shell exits 0 for a reason other than reaching `exit $verify_rc` (e.g. the base64/inner-sh pipeline swallows the inner exit), run_fix cannot distinguish 'checks re-ran and passed' from 'the verify step never executed'. The emitted marker is the explicit liveness signal but is never asserted.
scenarios: The inner script aborts (e.g. cd failure after fix) before printing GATEFIX_VERIFY_RC, yet buildah run returns 0 — run_fix would treat absence-of-failure as success.
dropped.suggested_fix: Return the parsed verify_rc from parse_fix_output and require both `code == 0` and a present `verify_rc == 0` in run_fix.
